g1-implement.title: G1 baseline + byte-identity harness: implement
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for G1 and dispatch constellation-implementer via run_crew.py. TASK: (1) Capture and paste the CURRENT green baseline -- run the six files of tests/unit/physics/instrument_panel/ plus tests/unit/physics/pilot/ on the pytest-capable interpreter, pasting the summary line and the HEAD hash it was run at. This baseline is NOT inherited from planning: every test invocation in the planning engagement was blocked by harness permission, so this is the first real measurement. (2) Create ONE new file, tests/unit/physics/instrument_panel/test_replication_axis_identity.py, that pins the EXACT current numeric output of the three public functions routing through the duplicated axis-grouping pass -- grand_two_way_center, per_driver_demean, and main_effect_margin_uncertainty -- as repr()-exact float literals captured from the UNMODIFIED module, asserted with '==' (NEVER pytest.approx: approx is blind to the last-ulp reordering regression this harness exists to catch; Python guarantees float(repr(x)) == x, so repr literals round-trip exactly). Cover at minimum: a balanced grid; a RAGGED grid (drivers missing different classes); an UNBALANCED grid (one driver with many more cells than another); a SINGLETON-ROW grid (a driver with exactly one cell, so _main_effect_se returns None); and a single-cell grid. Also assert the driver_se/class_se None-when-undefined convention and the thin-class flag survive. (2b) THE HARNESS MUST BE NON-VACUOUS -- cold-critic finding CC1: a grid built from exactly-representable binary values (0.5, 0.25, 2.0) gives bit-identical sums under ANY summation order, so such a harness would pass a genuinely reordered implementation and prove nothing. Use values that are NOT exact binary fractions (0.1, 0.7, 1/3, 1e-8 mixed with 1e8) and at least 4-5 cells per driver row and class column, so reordering the addition demonstrably moves the last ulp. PROVE the harness bites before handing it back: temporarily reverse the iteration order (or sum a shuffled copy) in a scratch edit, confirm at least one golden assertion FAILS, then revert the scratch edit. Report that demonstration in the IMPLEMENTER_RESULT -- an identity harness never shown to fail is an untested smoke alarm. (3) The new file MUST PASS AS WRITTEN against the current, unmodified replication.py -- G1 is green-on-arrival, and that is what makes it a valid baseline rather than a wish. Do NOT touch src/ in this gate (the scratch reordering in 2b is a temporary, reverted experiment, and git status must be clean of src/ changes when you return). Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.

g2-implement.title: G2 the dedup itself: implement
g2-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for G2 and dispatch constellation-implementer via run_crew.py. TASK: in src/physics/instrument_panel/replication.py ONLY, add one PRIVATE helper -- _axis_groups(grid: Grid) -> tuple[dict[object, list[float]], dict[object, list[float]]] -- that makes ONE pass over grid.items() and, per (driver, class_id) cell, appends float(value) to driver_rows.setdefault(driver, []) and class_cols.setdefault(class_id, []). Then route BOTH duplicated call sites through it: (1) _axis_means (currently replication.py:103-128) computes driver_mean = {d: sum(vals)/len(vals)} and class_mean = {c: sum(vals)/len(vals)} over the helper's output, and KEEPS ITS OWN separate single pass for the grand mean; (2) main_effect_margin_uncertainty (currently :425-429) deletes its two accumulation loops and calls the helper instead. THE BINDING NUMERIC CONSTRAINT: byte-identical output. Float addition is order-sensitive, so -- (a) the helper must visit cells in grid-iteration order, so each per-axis list is in the same order the current code accumulates; (b) the grand mean must remain its own left-to-right accumulation over the grid's values -- do NOT re-derive it by concatenating the driver rows (that reorders the addition) and do NOT switch to math.fsum, statistics.mean, or np.mean (all different algorithms with different rounding); (c) list order must be preserved because _main_effect_se feeds it to np.std(ddof=1). Docstrings: _axis_groups gets one stating it is the shared grouping pass and that its ORDER is load-bearing; _axis_means keeps its existing ragged-grid documented-approximation docstring verbatim. Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.

It is the module's deliberately-wrong NEGATIVE CONTROL and its readability is its value; widening the diff there costs Protected-Intent review budget for no behavioral gain. Route it through the helper only if that is a byte-identical no-op, otherwise leave it calling _axis_means exactly as today.

If byte-identity turns out NOT to be achievable under some sub-case, STOP and raise a blocker -- do not relax the harness to approx. A non-identical result invalidates the issue's own acceptance criterion and is the Commander's call, not the implementer's.
